pages.label: IT01
pages.title: Finite-Alphabet Entropy and Divergence
pages.summary: Fix finite probability, nats/bits, and explicit finite MI/CMI definitions before proving log-sum, KL equality, entropy chain, Fano, and Markov data processing.

pages.label: IT01-B
pages.title: Finite-Alphabet Entropy and Divergence — Examples
pages.summary: Verify binary entropy and KL calculations, including support failures, equality cases, and directionality; supplies no A-page prerequisite.

pages.label: IT02
pages.title: Measure-Theoretic Information and Conditioning
pages.summary: Define general law entropy as self-information I(X;X), distinct from differential entropy; define general MI by joint KL, standard-alphabet CMI by a same-marginal conditional-product law, and conditional KL with supplied kernels. Prove quantization, measurability, partition/variational, chain and equality results.

pages.label: IT02-B
pages.title: Measure-Theoretic Information and Conditioning — Examples
pages.summary: Expose null-version dependence of a naive reference-kernel construction and show why DPI conditions on the same variable.

pages.label: IT15
pages.title: Method of Types and Finite Large Deviations
pages.summary: Define empirical types and prove type-class counting/probability bounds before the finite-alphabet Sanov large-deviation theorem.

pages.label: IT15-B
pages.title: Method of Types and Finite Large Deviations — Examples
pages.summary: Compute binomial types and a finite Sanov tail, keeping polynomial prefactors visible.

pages.label: IT16
pages.title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing
pages.summary: Define finite f- and Rényi divergences with support/zero conventions, prove finite data processing and the KL limit, and relate KL to the explicitly oriented testing function.

pages.label: IT16-B
pages.title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing — Examples
pages.summary: Check binary divergences, likelihood-ratio thresholding, and support singularities.

pages.label: IT03
pages.title: Prefix Codes and Finite Lossless Coding
pages.summary: Define finite uniquely decodable and prefix codes, prove binary Kraft–McMillan and Shannon/Huffman bounds, and distinguish ideal-real interval coding from a finite-register coder with exact counter and termination contracts.

pages.label: IT03-B
pages.title: Prefix Codes and Finite Lossless Coding — Examples
pages.summary: Work exact code-tree and Huffman examples, including a uniquely decodable non-prefix code.

pages.label: IT04
pages.title: IID Lossless Source Coding and the AEP
pages.summary: Prove the finite-alphabet IID information AEP and fixed-length lossless coding converse/achievability with explicit error and rate limits.

pages.label: IT04-B
pages.title: IID Lossless Source Coding and the AEP — Examples
pages.summary: Compute Bernoulli typical-set sizes and isolate the hypotheses behind information-spectrum convergence.

pages.label: IT05
pages.title: Stationary Ergodic Sources and Universal Coding
pages.summary: Separate general limsup, stationary limits, nonergodic componentwise SMB, ergodic constant-rate SMB, and AMS extensions. Prove expected LZ78 rate universality for stationary finite-alphabet sources; retain distinct individual-sequence LZ78 and stationary-ergodic LZ77 claims with explicit source/proof obligations pending their primary-paper supplement.

pages.label: IT05-B
pages.title: Stationary Ergodic Sources and Universal Coding — Examples
pages.summary: Compare IID and Markov source rates, show a nonstationary boundary case, and trace LZ78 parsing on a finite word.

pages.label: IT06
pages.title: Rate Distortion and Lossy Source Coding
pages.summary: Define operational and single-letter distortion-rate quantities, prove the finite memoryless theorem and scoped formulae, and supply a certified finite-alphabet optimization algorithm.

pages.label: IT06-B
pages.title: Rate Distortion and Lossy Source Coding — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate finite and Gaussian distortion curves and record why unrestricted continuous-output density assumptions fail.

pages.label: IT07
pages.title: Discrete Memoryless Channel Capacity
pages.summary: Define a general sequence of channel kernels before its finite DMC subclass, then define fixed-length codes and error criteria and prove finite-DMC capacity/strong-converse results with alphabet and cost assumptions stated.

pages.label: IT07-B
pages.title: Discrete Memoryless Channel Capacity — Examples
pages.summary: Compute BSC/BEC capacities and contrast average and maximal error criteria on finite channels.

pages.label: IT08
pages.title: Cost-Constrained, Gaussian, and Feedback Channels
pages.summary: State scalar/vector Gaussian channel and cost models, define differential entropy only for the density/moment class where its integral is well defined, and prove Gaussian and feedback claims under explicit power/covariance/memorylessness conditions.

pages.label: IT08-B
pages.title: Cost-Constrained, Gaussian, and Feedback Channels — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate the AWGN and water-filling formulae and show that a finite capacity supremum need not have an attaining input law.

pages.label: IT09
pages.title: Finite-Blocklength Bounds and Reliability
pages.summary: Develop one-shot bounds with exact type-I/type-II conventions, then state dispersion and exponent results with nondegeneracy and coding-error premises.

pages.label: IT09-B
pages.title: Finite-Blocklength Bounds and Reliability — Examples
pages.summary: Evaluate one-shot bounds and demonstrate the distinction between a random-codebook expectation and maximal error of each codeword.

pages.label: IT17
pages.title: Point-to-Point Source–Channel Separation
pages.summary: Define a joint source–channel code and prove lossless and lossy separation only for finite memoryless models, asymptotic block criteria, and the stated rate-distortion attainment conditions.

pages.label: IT17-B
pages.title: Point-to-Point Source–Channel Separation — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate a finite rate budget and show why asymptotic separation does not assert finite-block or zero-delay equivalence.

pages.label: IT10
pages.title: Distributed Source Coding
pages.summary: Define finite IID multiterminal source codes and prove the k-source Slepian–Wolf region by all-subset converse and random-binning achievability.

pages.label: IT10-B
pages.title: Distributed Source Coding — Examples
pages.summary: Compute two-source Slepian–Wolf corners and check the random-binning independence hypothesis.

pages.label: IT18
pages.title: Lossy Source Coding with Side Information
pages.summary: State the finite-alphabet memoryless Wyner–Ziv theorem and cardinality limits; distinguish its exact single-encoder region from the Berger–Tung inner bound for multiple encoders.

pages.label: IT18-B
pages.title: Lossy Source Coding with Side Information — Examples
pages.summary: Compare decoder-only and encoder/decoder side information and label multiterminal regions as inner bounds.

pages.label: IT11
pages.title: Multiuser Channel Networks
pages.summary: Prove product-input DM/AWGN MAC and degraded broadcast regions, then state the exact DMC feedback no-gain result, Ozarow feedback region, Cover–Leung inner bound, and correlated-source MAC sufficient condition with separate operational models.

pages.label: IT11-B
pages.title: Multiuser Channel Networks — Examples
pages.summary: Plot or calculate finite exact special regions and demonstrate the independent private-message input law.

pages.label: IT19
pages.title: Relay and Interference Channel Bounds
pages.summary: Define causal relay/two-way models and directed information before use; prove named relay/NNC inner bounds and cut-set outer bounds, the sharp sourced Gaussian multicast gap, feedback relay special case, exact strong-interference region, and Gaussian two-user approximation. Record general relay scope without asserting a current open-problem status absent a literature review.

pages.label: IT19-B
pages.title: Relay and Interference Channel Bounds — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate a relay bound gap and an exact strong-interference region; show the limits of the regime hypothesis.

pages.label: IT12
pages.title: Secrecy and Information Privacy
pages.summary: Define weak/strong secrecy, leakage and finite-source privacy; prove the finite DMC wiretap auxiliary formula (and its degraded simplification), channel-resolvability and leftover-hash bounds with exact leakage and error metrics.

pages.label: IT12-B
pages.title: Secrecy and Information Privacy — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate a finite wiretap example and distinguish leakage normalizations and model-dependent privacy criteria.

pages.label: IT13
pages.title: Quantum Information Measures
pages.summary: Define finite-dimensional quantum entropy and support-sensitive relative entropy in the root convention, then prove entropy identities, Holevo measurement bounds, and channel data processing.

pages.label: IT13-B
pages.title: Quantum Information Measures — Examples
pages.summary: Compute qubit entropy and Holevo information and expose the quantum relative-entropy support boundary.

pages.label: IT20
pages.title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity
pages.summary: Prove a finite operator ladder from inverse compression and resolvent Jensen through support regularization and joint convexity, then derive QRE data processing, strong subadditivity, conditional MI nonnegativity, and Holevo measurement bounds.

pages.label: IT20-B
pages.title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity — Examples
pages.summary: Check finite matrix cases and separate fidelity/trace-distance contractivity from QRE data processing.

pages.label: IT14
pages.title: Quantum Source Compression and Classical Communication over Quantum Channels
pages.summary: Prove finite-dimensional Schumacher compression and the HSW classical capacity theorem for finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channels.

pages.label: IT14-B
pages.title: Quantum Source Compression and Classical Communication over Quantum Channels — Examples
pages.summary: Work qubit compression and binary cq examples, including why a fixed POVM need not attain the Holevo quantity.

pages.label: IT21
pages.title: Quantum Channel Capacities and Entanglement Assistance
pages.summary: Prove regularized coherent/private information capacity formulae, the additive entanglement-assisted formula, and exact degradable/erasure cases without claiming general single-letter additivity.

pages.label: IT21-B
pages.title: Quantum Channel Capacities and Entanglement Assistance — Examples
pages.summary: Compute erasure-channel regimes and contrast an exact degradable formula with the general regularized capacity.

pages.label: IT22
pages.title: Quantum Key Distribution and Composable Secrecy
pages.summary: Define a finite protocol, authenticated public transcript, abort-aware ideal-real trace-distance criterion and correctness error, then prove the stated composable sum-of-errors implication.

pages.label: IT22-B
pages.title: Quantum Key Distribution and Composable Secrecy — Examples
pages.summary: Calculate abort-weighted trace distance for a finite key protocol and separate key secrecy from correctness.

pages.label: IT23
pages.title: Finite Quantization, Lloyd Iteration, and Compact Companders
pages.summary: Finite empirical optimization and restricted compact one-dimensional high-rate asymptotics with exact algorithm contracts.

pages.label: IT23-B
pages.title: Finite Quantization, Lloyd Iteration, and Compact Companders — Examples
pages.summary: Worked exact computations and counterexamples; no later A-page prerequisite.

pages.label: IT24
pages.title: Finite Trellises, Viterbi, and Sequence Decoding
pages.summary: Finite layered dynamic programming and exact HMM sequence MAP, with unreachable-state and zero-evidence boundaries.

pages.label: IT24-B
pages.title: Finite Trellises, Viterbi, and Sequence Decoding — Examples
pages.summary: Worked exact computations and counterexamples; no later A-page prerequisite.
